reader_summary.headline: Mohnish Pabrai shares his investing secrets, lunch with Buffett, and advice on memory chips.
reader_summary.overview: Mohnish Pabrai explains how he paid a large fee to learn from Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger. He warns that South Korea's shrinking population will hurt its economy. He also shares his strict checklist for finding safe, boring investments that trade cheaply.

key_points.text: Pabrai paid $650,000 for a lunch with Warren Buffett because he felt it was a fair tuition fee for learning.
key_points.evidence_quote: I had made more than $70 million directly from applying the principles of Warren Buffett. I felt like a tuition bill was due.

key_points.text: Investors should hold existing memory chip stocks but avoid buying new ones because the market is too crowded.
key_points.evidence_quote: if you already own it, don't sell it. But if you don't own it, don't buy it. So now is not the time to buy.

key_points.text: Avoid debt and buy boring businesses that are hated and trading far below their actual value.
key_points.evidence_quote: Please don't buy shiny objects. Please don't buy what is loved. Please buy what is hated and unloved.

key_points.text: Your personality and investment style are fixed by your early life experiences and will not change.
key_points.evidence_quote: The way I was when I was five years old, and the way I'm going to be when I'm 95 years old, is the same.
